read_scope.notes: Read all 22 PDF pages, including the complete main text, references and Appendices A–G, from a layout-preserving extraction. Visually inspected every rendered PDF page, including Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–12. Consulted the frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to verify the abstract, score definitions, results wording and conclusion. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth for the intended reader. Extraction and rendering used the isolated directory /tmp/editorial-r31-b-jzYMKu. Did not inspect other reviews, earlier manuscripts, progress records or external research.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise prose with only localized compression. Section 4.1 (p. 5) explains contrasts and the two scores in ordinary language before the equations; the lightness example and three idealized generators make the terminology concrete. Qualifications are attached to the claims they limit rather than left for the final limitations section. The final numerical paragraph of Section 5.2 is a small exception: it states the shared-versus-generic ratios without an equally direct verbal takeaway.
score_reasons.structure: The question, six-condition experiment, measurement target, score intuition, formal definitions and findings form a coherent progression. The main text ends on p. 10 and communicates the study without requiring the substantial optional appendices. Declared comparisons and retrospective diagnostics remain visibly distinct, including the source-correction table. Section 5.4 gives separate interpretations to scene averaging and magnitude calibration. Only the conclusion could give slightly less closing emphasis to an already explained individual model comparison.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract is standalone and communicates the experiment, main findings and perceptual limit. Sections 3–4 specify the finite reference target, development scaling, experimental arms and meaning of D=0, D=1 and beta=1 without assuming repository knowledge. The main figures have usable legends and interpretive captions: Figure 1 makes the controls concrete, Figure 2 magnifies nearby painter positions, and Figure 3 labels both alignment and error benchmarks. The generic-arm comparison at the end of Section 5.2 would benefit from one clearer plain-language interpretation, but no important understanding gap remains.
score_reasons.engagement: The distinction between a visible name response and correctly labeled painter differences is consequential and sustained. Concrete contrasts such as GPT Image 2 versus FLUX, weak Monet–Sisley alignment, and the Nano Banana 2 scene-averaging reversal give the numerical results a discernible narrative. The image grid and focused pair heatmaps reward inspection. Momentum softens slightly in the un-interpreted shared/generic numerical paragraph and in the conclusion’s return to one source-sensitivity comparison; these are localized refinements rather than broad pacing problems.

strengths: Section 4.1 (p. 5) uses the observed Monet–Sisley lightness gap before introducing stacked feature geometry, then explains the no-distinction, exact-match and doubled-contrast benchmarks. This is effective intuition before notation.

The primary finding in Section 5.1 and Table 2 (pp. 6–7) separates positive aligned response, the lowest point estimate and statistically resolved model differences. It explicitly says that no model is established to beat the no-distinction predictor.

Figure 1 (p. 4) places all six conditions in each model row and clearly distinguishes illustrative reference works from generator inputs or matched compositions. Figures 2–3 make the aggregate-versus-pair distinction inspectable without implying perceptual validation.
Section 5.4 and Table 4 (p. 9) explain why averaging scenes and shrinking contrasts change error ordering, while making clear that calibration changes feature vectors and not images.

Section 5.5 and Table 5 (pp. 9–10) openly display the comparison that becomes unresolved after source correction and the retrospective status of the newly positive GPT Image 1 comparison. The limitations and availability statements retain the AI-audit and exact-pixel restrictions.

findings.issue: The generic oil-painting control receives a squared-magnitude range and a cosine range, but the paragraph stops before directly stating what those estimates reveal about the common named response. Elsewhere the manuscript translates its numerical comparisons more explicitly.
findings.reader_effect: A new reader can understand the two quantities but must supply the useful takeaway: the common response under names is larger than, and broadly directed along, the response to the generic painting clause. This slightly underuses a control arm central to the motivation.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the two sentences with an equally compact interpretive version, preserving the baseline, scene averaging and correction: “The shared named response is larger than, and broadly aligned with, the generic oil-painting response: repeat-corrected squared-magnitude ratios are 1.96–4.14 and cosines .689–.930 (1 means parallel), using scene averages and the same artist-free baseline.” Keep the appendix reference. This requires no new evidence or page growth.

findings.issue: The short conclusion returns to the particular Sunburst–FLUX adjusted interval after Section 5.5 and Table 5 have already explained it clearly. That individual retrospective comparison receives unusually specific emphasis at the end of an otherwise general synthesis.
findings.reader_effect: The ending briefly shifts attention from the broader evaluation lesson to recalling one model-specific sensitivity result. The central conclusion remains clear, but its final emphasis could be sharper.
findings.suggested_change: Compress that sentence to “Source correction preserves FLUX’s lowest uncalibrated estimate while changing which model differences are resolved.” Retain the exact Sunburst comparison in Section 5.5 and Table 5 and retain the existing final sentence. This preserves the evidence and shortens the paper.

summary: An excellent editorial presentation of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main narrative, controls, metrics and findings are readily understandable to a graduate-level reader without project-specific knowledge, and the figures and captions support that narrative. Only localized improvements to interpretation and closing emphasis remain; no substantial restructuring or additional experiments are needed.
